title: Detect Vitest CPU starvation that begins after startup preflight
outcome: A full serialized Vitest run passed startup resource admission, then an unrelated sorted_list_stress_tests process began consuming up to ~425% CPU and system load reached 37 on 8 logical CPUs. App.control-panel.openers timed out at 11.4s under the unchanged 10s limit. An immediate focused command was rejected before tests: median 790.8ms wall / 100.8ms CPU (12.7% CPU, ratio 7.84 > 3). The product/test assertion did not fail; the environment starved the runner after the one-shot preflight. Add a bounded mid-run/per-file resource admission mechanism that reports resource starvation explicitly without retries, quarantine, or timeout inflation.
acceptance: A CPU-starved serialized file that begins after Vitest startup is rejected with the explicit resource diagnostic before a normal test timeout is misreported; normal runs retain the 10-second timeout and add negligible overhead; focused tests cover pass and reject paths.
